what_it_is: The calls of an association study that Python and TypeScript both
refuse, the values that neither refuses because both read them as a
number, and the three that TypeScript alone refuses. It is the one file
of this directory that no reference program wrote: the others are what
plink2, GMMAT and rrBLUP answered, and this is a list the two test
suites read so that neither layer can refuse something the other
accepts without this file saying that it does.
`case` is the call, which each suite writes in its own language over
the worked example of `docs/specs/gwas.md`; a case that a suite has no
call for fails that suite, which is what makes the file bind. `match`
is a regular expression that the message of both layers has to hold, so
it is written out of the words the two share and not out of one of
them: the names of the arguments differ between the two languages, and
so does the quoting of a name in a message.
`refusals` are the calls both layers refuse. `coercions` are the calls
where a value that is not a number reaches the study as one, with
`float` in Python and `Number` in TypeScript: each of them is the
worked example written another way, so each suite asserts the null
model that example gives and no case there has a `match`.
`refused_in_typescript_alone` is the one divergence the spec settled,
on 23 September 2026. Python says that an individual has no phenotype
with a name that the series has not, with `None` or with NaN;
TypeScript says it with a key that the object has not, and that is the
only way to say it there, because `Number` turns `null` into 0 and
`undefined` into NaN and a NaN phenotype would leave a typo out of the
study in silence. Each suite asserts its own half: the TypeScript one
the refusal of `match`, and the Python one a study of the five
individuals that `i2` is not among.
